title: introduce-invocation-snapshot-compactifier-and-alert-sedimentation
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Long-running investigations frequently require iterating through hundreds of large spans and full invocation traces. This PR introduces an invocation snapshot compactifier, a span paginator API for the Observability UI, and an "alert sedimentation" mechanism that reduces alert noise by consolidating repeated token-cost/latency signals into a single actionable event. The goal is to reduce UI load, lower storage amplification for sampled traces, and make alerting more interpretable for SREs and product owners.

Summary of changes (high-level):
- Add a compact indexer service (telemetry/snapshot-compactifier) that consumes sampled invocation payloads, extracts a compact keyset (heatmap anchors, token-count signature, route fingerprint), and writes small snapshot blobs to the indexed store. The compact blobs are ~80-150 bytes per invocation vs 5-20 KB previously for sampled traces.
- Implement a span paginator endpoint (observability/api/paginator) that returns ordered span slices for a given invocation snapshot id. The paginator supports cursor-based forward/backward paging and a streaming mode for UI progressive rendering.
- Add "alert sedimentation" (observability/alerts/sediment) policy that groups successive token-cost or latency alerts from the same route+fingerprint into one escalated alert with a summarized runbook link. Sedimentation windows are configurable per-team.
- UI: dashboard tweaks to invocation list and a new compact snapshot preview card (webapp/dashboards/CompactSnapshotCard.tsx) that renders metadata and a short timeline without pulling full spans. Pager integrated into the invocation detail view.
- Migration: a background job to bootstrap compact index entries from last 7 days of sampled traces.
- Tests: unit tests for indexer logic, integration tests for paginator cursor behavior, e2e preview smoke tests for the CompactSnapshotCard.

Commits:
- 3f8b2c9: initial compactifier service scaffolding and proto for compact snapshot blobs
- a7d9f11: add paginator API and cursor implementation; add integration tests
- b5e6a2d: alert sedimentation policy, UI preview card, alerting docs and migration job

Behavioral notes and constraints:
- The indexer runs in best-effort mode; snapshots are additive. We do not delete original spans or sampled traces as part of this PR. The compact blobs are intended to be a low-cost, quick-preview path for most investigations.
- Paginator returns stable cursors tied to compact snapshot generation timestamp; cursors expire after 48 hours. This avoids unbounded retention on paginated cursors and simplifies garbage collection.
- Alert sedimentation uses a sliding decay: repeated alerts within window are collapsed; after stable recurrence above escalation threshold we produce a single parent alert with a summarized evidence payload (compact snapshot reference).

Testing and rollout strategy:
- Canary: roll indexer to observability-canary with a 1% sample of sampled traces for 48h. Monitor compact index hit-rate and UI render latencies.
- If compact index write error rates exceed 0.5% in canary, automatically scale back to 0% via feature flag.
- Gradual rollout to prod over 2 weeks with telemetry on: compact_index_write_success, paginator_latency_p95, alert_sedimentation_rate.

Impact on cost: Compact snapshots reduce per-invocation storage for sampled traces by ~95% in the traced sample pipeline; initial estimates show 12-18% reduction in observability storage TCO for teams with high sampling. There is minor added CPU for the indexer (profiled on n2-standard equivalent, ~5% CPU on canary).

Backward compatibility: Paginator API is additive. Existing trace consumers and alerting rules continue to function unchanged unless teams opt into sedimentation. Feature flag "obs.compact_snapshot_v1" gated.

CI summary: initial CI run failed lint on webapp formatting and a race in paginator_test. Fixes included in second commit. Final CI: build/pass, unit/pass, integration/pass, e2e/pass. See CI details below.

Review conversation (abbreviated, single continuous narrative):
- Arjun Rao (reviewer): "High-level this looks great; can you justify the 48h cursor TTL? Is that long enough for cross-team handoffs?"
- Maya Patel (author): "We picked 48h to limit GC complexity and disk pointers; teams needing longer handoffs can pin the invocation or export full trace. We can extend TTL per-team if necessary — added a config flag in terraform."
- Lena Thomason (reviewer): "alert sedimentation is promising but risk of masking flakey incidents. How do we ensure we don't hide a real regression?"
- Maya Patel: "Sedimentation keeps an evidence link and increments an internal recurrence counter. If recurrence crosses escalation thresholds we escalate with a richer payload. Also added an operator opt-out label to disable sedimentation for critical routes."
- QA (reviewer): "paginator test flake reproduced locally; suggest deterministic clock usage in cursor encoding."
- Maya Patel: "Addressed: cursor encodes a trimmed timestamp and monotonic sequence; used test clock in tests. Re-ran CI and integration tests now stable."
- SRE (approver): "Approving for canary. Please add a runbook snippet for what to do when compact index lag > 5 minutes."
- Maya Patel: "Added runbook snippet into telemetry/snapshot-compactifier/README.md and linked from observability runbooks."

CI details (single line summary): "CI: build/pass; lint/pass; unit/pass; integration/pass (one rerun due to paginator_test flake); e2e/pass; security-scan/pass; deploy/canary/pass"

Merge outcome: Merged via squash-and-merge after approvals from SRE and two reviewers. Release notes entry added.

Release notes: "Add compact invocation snapshot indexer, UI preview card, paginator API, and alert sedimentation policy — reduces observability storage for sampled traces and improves investigation latency. Feature gated and rolled out to canary."

Related Linear items and tickets: "ENG-1498, ENG-2301"

Notes for oncall and pager teams: "If you see sudden drop in sampled-trace render rate or compact_index_write_failures > 0.5% for 30m, run the diagnostic in README and disable obs.compact_snapshot_v1 via the feature flag. For sedimentation mis-grouping, use team label 'sediment:disabled' on route config to bypass."
release_notes: Add compact invocation snapshot indexer, UI preview card, paginator API, and alert sedimentation policy. Feature gated; initial canary rollout. Reduces observability storage and improves investigation latency.
